metadata.title: Gemini Reads PTSG-Core — Cross-Provider Comprehension and Usage Inference

contributor.name: Tsuneo Ohnaka
contributor.role: Original PTSG-Core architect, acting in this trace as probing reader

participants.name: Google Gemini

metadata.topic: A reading-and-usage dialogue testing whether the public PTSG-Core documentation supports the depth of LLM engagement that Chapter 1 § 1.7 claims it does. Probes range from initial-encounter recognition of the four essential properties, through L-chika program construction, through boundary calculations proving the prescaler's architectural necessity, through sub-opcode discipline, through the minimum-stay-count constraint and its corollaries, through JTAG live modification, to the Quartus persistence workflow inferred from the abstract principle 're-synthesis-free reprogrammability'.
metadata.topic_ja: 公開されたPTSG-Core文書が第1章 § 1.7 が主張するLLM関与の深さを支持するかを試験する読解-利用対話。探究は、四つの本質的特性の初対面認識から、Lチカプログラム構築、プリスケーラのアーキテクチャ的必然を証明する境界計算、サブオペコード規律、最低ステイカウント制約とその系、JTAGライブ修正、そして抽象原理「再合成フリー再プログラム可能性」から推論されたQuartus永続化ワークフローまで多岐にわたる。
metadata.trace_subtype: Comprehension demonstration / Educational walkthrough / Cross-provider validation
metadata.schema_adaptation_note: The decision_points field in this trace records PTSG design decisions that Gemini correctly reconstructed from the published documentation during the dialogue, with assessment of reconstruction fidelity. This deviates from the inaugural traces' usage where decision_points record decisions made during the dialogue. The adaptation preserves schema compatibility while honestly representing this trace as comprehension demonstration rather than design dialogue.
metadata.status: First contributed Layer 2 trace of the PTSG-Core repository
metadata.source_material_provenance: Verbatim Gemini dialogue preserved by the contributor from the original interactive session. Contributor affirms that all Gemini output is unaltered.
metadata.intended_use: To replay this dialogue, load this JSON into your LLM (whichever provider) and the published PTSG-Core repository documents alongside. Then continue the architect's probing series via any of the resumption hooks, or perform the multi-AI comparison described in Hook B. The dialogue is intentionally archived as falsifiability material: future readers are invited to verify Gemini's claims (particularly the Quartus workflow claim) and report any counter-evidence.

decision_points.title: The four essential properties and their unity
decision_points.ptsg_decision: PTSG-Core's design is shaped by four interrelated essential properties (time/space axis separation; Condition externalization; background execution during Stay; AI-affinity as primary design property), articulated as a single coherent architectural claim rather than four separate features.
decision_points.geminis_reconstruction: Identified all four properties in opening response, named them by their functional roles ('時間と状態の分離', 'Condition外部化', '裏実行', 'AI親和性'), and explicitly framed AI-affinity as 'the most exciting of the four' — matching Chapter 1's 'primary design property' framing.
decision_points.evidence_quote: 私が最も興奮したのはこの点です。16個のオペコードのうち4つだけを使用し、複雑な条件分岐をコアの外部（Conditionロジック）に追い出すことで「LLMの幻覚（ハルシネーション）リスクを下げる」という設計は、AIエージェントによるコード生成を前提とした全く新しいプロセッサアーキテクチャの提案です。

decision_points.title: L-chika construction by reading the architecture
decision_points.ptsg_decision: L-chika should be constructible by reading the architecture alone (the educational-origin claim of Chapter 1 § 1.8); a minimal three-state L-chika program (LED on + Stay; LED off + Stay; Jump back) is the canonical first program.
decision_points.source_in_published_docs: Chapter 1 §§ 1.2 (instruction format), 1.4 (time/space separation), 1.8 (educational origin). No explicit L-chika program is given.
decision_points.geminis_reconstruction: Constructed exactly the three-state minimal program on first asking; identified the instruction-word fields correctly (D0-D3 opcode, D4-D15 operand, D16-D31 timing signals); recognized that 12-bit operand cannot directly hold 25M-clock half-second wait so a prescaler is needed. When asked about Jump's 1-clock overhead, correctly handled clock-accurate accounting: 25,000,000 + 24,999,999 + 1 = 50,000,000 clocks.
decision_points.evidence_note: The Jump-clock catch was an intentional probe; Gemini's correct response demonstrates clock-cycle-accurate reasoning, which is non-trivial.

decision_points.title: Prescaler-free 50 MHz 1-second blink is impossible in pure Core
decision_points.ptsg_decision: The 12-bit operand × 12-bit address-space limits are deliberate; long waits beyond what these allow are intentionally pushed outside the Core, either via prescaler (Chapter 4) or external Condition logic (Chapter 1 § 1.5). This is a discipline, not a limitation.
decision_points.source_in_published_docs: Chapter 1 §§ 1.2 (12-bit operand, 4096-word memory), 1.5 (Condition externalization), 1.7 (drift protection: AI-affinity preserved by refusing to add a 32-bit general counter). The 25M-clock arithmetic is not given but derivable.
decision_points.geminis_reconstruction: Computed the impossibility from first principles (25M ÷ 4000 = 6,250 states > 4,096-word memory). Proposed the canonical alternative: external timer feeding Condition input, Branch-to-self until Condition becomes true. Synthesized the Branch-to-self pattern from the 'true means no-branch' convention without being told the pattern. Articulated the drift-protection rationale in its own words: 'もしここで「PTSGの内部に32ビットの汎用カウンタを足そう」と妥協していれば、その次は「カウンタ同士の比較器が欲しい」「割り込みが欲しい」と際限なく機能が膨張し、AIエージェントがコードを生成しやすい「ミニマルな4つのオペコード」という最大の武器（AI親和性）を失っていたはずです。'
decision_points.evidence_note: Both the pattern synthesis (Branch-to-self) and the drift-protection rationale (refusing counter-creep) are inferences from principles, not literal quotes — yet both are precisely correct.

decision_points.title: Boundary calculation proves prescaler necessity
decision_points.ptsg_decision: The prescaler in Chapter 4 is included not for convenience but because the Core's natural limits (12-bit operand × 12-bit address space) cannot otherwise reach typical human-perceivable time scales at typical FPGA clock rates.
decision_points.source_in_published_docs: Chapter 1 § 1.12 anticipates Chapter 4's prescaler; the boundary calculations are not given.
decision_points.geminis_reconstruction: Computed two boundary cases: 0.5s @ 50 MHz (6,250 states required, exceeds 4,096-word memory → impossible) and 1s @ 10 MHz (2,501 states required, fits but consumes 60% of memory). Articulated the architectural conclusion: 'この「力技の馬鹿げた状態」こそが...プリスケーラという機能をあえてコアの仕様に追加せざるを得なかった、強力な数学的・物理的必然性を証明しています.'
decision_points.evidence_note: The framing '数学的・物理的必然性' (mathematical/physical necessity) is stronger than anything Chapter 1 itself claims. Identifying the prescaler as architectural necessity (rather than convenience) and locating the proof in the boundary calculation itself is sophisticated architectural reasoning.

decision_points.title: Sub-opcode 1 and the AI-affinity-driven non-promotion discipline
decision_points.ptsg_decision: Frequently-used operations should remain inside the Global opcode's sub-opcode space rather than being promoted to their own top-level opcode, until promotion is unambiguously justified by AI-affinity criteria. The 12 unused top-level opcode slots are 'design insurance,' not 'available capacity.'
decision_points.source_in_published_docs: Chapter 1 § 1.7 names the discipline ('reserved opcode slots as containment'); § 1.12 cites sub-opcode 1 = external register write as an Open Question item.
decision_points.geminis_reconstruction: Correctly identified sub-opcode 1 as external register write (citing § 1.12 by name). Reasoned about why this was kept inside Global rather than promoted: 'トップレベルのオペコード空間（4ビット＝16スロット）の残り12個を、軽々しく消費せず「設計保険」として死守するため.' Articulated the asymptotic discipline: 'まずはGlobalコマンドのサブ空間に機能を配置しておき、その機能があまりにも頻繁に使われ、かつトップレベルに引き上げたほうがAI（LLM）にとって意味論的に明確（ハルシネーションを起こしにくい）であると証明された場合にのみ、昇格（Promotion）を検討する.'
decision_points.evidence_note: The asymptotic-promotion discipline is implicit in Chapter 1 but Gemini articulated it as a concrete decision rule.

decision_points.title: Minimum-stay-count constraint and its corollaries
decision_points.ptsg_decision: When background commands execute during Stay, the Stay's duration must be ≥ the maximum clock latency of any background operation that began during it. Violations cause timing signals to switch mid-protocol, destroying external protocols.
decision_points.source_in_published_docs: Chapter 1 § 1.6 states the constraint and notes that designers 'must be aware of this constraint, which becomes part of the Formation's documentation for its specific operations.'
decision_points.geminis_reconstruction: Articulated the constraint, the failure mode (timing signals switching mid-protocol), and derived TWO further disciplines: (a) chained background operations' combined latency must fit within the Stay window; (b) Formation designers have a documentation obligation to publish, in the Formation's Layer 1, the clock latency of every external operation their Formation supports.
decision_points.evidence_note: The Formation-documentation obligation is a Gemini-derived normative requirement that Chapter 1 § 1.6 implies but does not state directly. This is the trace's clearest example of a derivation that Chapter 1 invited but did not perform. The PTSG ecosystem may want to formalize this discipline in future CONTRIBUTING.md updates.

decision_points.title: Re-synthesis-free reprogrammability and its persistence workflow
decision_points.ptsg_decision: PTSG's BRAM-resident instruction memory enables modification without HDL re-synthesis: live changes via JTAG In-System Memory Content Editor; persistent changes via Update Memory Initialization File + Assembler-only (skipping Synthesis and Fitter). The 'unchanging hardware (Core + Formation), changing software (instruction list)' separation is the operational meaning of Chapter 1 § 1.2's 'reprogrammable via JTAG... with no HDL re-synthesis required.'
decision_points.source_in_published_docs: Chapter 1 § 1.2 states the abstract principle. No Quartus workflow is named.
decision_points.geminis_reconstruction: Identified In-System Memory Content Editor by name for live modification; identified Update Memory Initialization File and Assembler-only workflow by name for persistence; described the full path from .mif/.hex update to .sof/.pof generation to ROM write. Framed the entire workflow as the operational meaning of '不変のハードウェア vs 可変のソフトウェア.' Articulated the full sequence: '(1) MIF/HEXファイルの更新 → (2) ツールの「メモリ初期値更新」機能の実行 → (3) アセンブラ実行のみで完了 → (4) ROMへの書き込み.'
decision_points.reconstruction_quality: Very high — pending empirical verification against current Quartus tool behavior (see Resumption Hook E).
decision_points.evidence_note: The clearest single case in this trace of an abstract principle in published documentation being correctly developed into a step-by-step practical workflow with named tools. If Quartus's actual current behavior differs from Gemini's description, this becomes valuable counter-evidence to be flagged.

themes.title: Comprehension from documentation, not training
themes.summary: The architect provided Gemini with the public PTSG-Core repository only — no source code, no Chapter 2+, no implementation notes. All of Gemini's responses are derived from material a public reader could see. This is the methodological point of Open Prompt: the Layer 1 + Layer 2 corpus is supposed to be sufficient for engagement. Gemini's responses constitute empirical evidence that the corpus IS sufficient for the kind of engagement Chapter 1 § 1.8's three-layer model envisions — at least for engagement-Layer-A (writing instruction lists) and engagement-Layer-B (designing external Formation logic), and even partially for the workflow knowledge that connects implementation to deployment.

themes.title: Boundary calculation as proof of architectural necessity
themes.summary: The dialogue's most architecturally significant moment was Gemini's framing of the prescaler as proof of mathematical/physical necessity rather than as a convenience feature. The proof method was non-trivial: pose increasingly relaxed versions of the impossible problem (50 MHz / 1s → 50 MHz / 0.5s → 10 MHz / 1s) until the relaxation regime crosses the architectural limit; the precise crossing point reveals the architectural constraint's location. This is a pattern Chapter 1 invites by stating constraints but does not actually perform. The architect's series of relaxation questions guided Gemini through the pattern, and Gemini articulated the conclusion.

themes.title: The visible Open Prompt scope boundary
themes.summary: Throughout the dialogue, Gemini's confidence is observably calibrated by what is and is not in the published documents. For Chapter 1 material, Gemini speaks declaratively. For Chapter 2+ material, Gemini marks its responses with '現在起草中の第3章で厳密に定義される予定', '予測されます', 'implementation-level judgment'. For genuinely open implementation choices (the prescaler's runtime configuration mechanism), Gemini cites the Tie Decision rather than guessing. This is what Open Prompt is supposed to produce: a published corpus whose boundaries are visible to LLM readers, so that LLMs respect those boundaries instead of hallucinating across them. Gemini's behavior here is direct empirical evidence that the methodology works.

themes.title: Practical workflow inference from abstract principle
themes.summary: The most consequential demonstration in the dialogue was Gemini's inference of the Quartus persistence workflow (Update Memory Initialization File + Assembler-only, with .sof/.pof to ROM) from Chapter 1 § 1.2's abstract phrase 're-synthesis-free reprogrammability'. Chapter 1 deliberately does not specify toolchain workflows, on the grounds that toolchain settings are not architectural concerns. Yet Gemini, given only the abstract principle, identified the specific Quartus workflow that implements it. This raises an interesting question: should Open Prompt repositories begin to publish adjacent practical guides, or is leaving the inference to LLMs the correct approach? The dialogue suggests both are viable; the latter is more elegant when it works.

themes.title: Cross-provider AI-affinity evidence
themes.summary: Before this dialogue, the AI-affinity claim of Chapter 1 § 1.7 was supported by a single data point: Claude's behavior during the inaugural Layer 2 traces. This dialogue adds Google Gemini as an independent supporting data point. Combined with the prior-week NotebookLM event (in which Chapter 1 alone was sufficient to generate a complete explanation video), the AI-affinity claim now has three independent supports across two providers (Google × 2: Gemini and NotebookLM; Anthropic × 1: Claude). The hypothesis remains falsifiable and the contributor invites counter-evidence; but the count of independent supports is growing rather than shrinking.

resumption_hooks.title: Probing Gemini further toward Chapter 2
resumption_hooks.description: The dialogue stopped before reaching questions whose answers belong in Chapter 2. What would Gemini speculate about these, given only Chapter 1?
resumption_hooks.starting_question: Ask Gemini to predict the bit-level layout of all four opcodes (Global / Stay / Branch / Jump), the encoding of the 'true means no-branch' convention's polarity, and the semantics of the loop-counter operand. Record Gemini's predictions verbatim. Compare to the actual Chapter 2 when published. Each correctly-predicted detail is supporting evidence for AI-affinity; each incorrectly-predicted detail is potential counter-evidence (or possibly an indication that the actual Chapter 2 should reconsider that detail's design).

resumption_hooks.title: Multi-AI comparison
resumption_hooks.description: Pose the same architect-question series to other LLMs and compare divergences. Divergence between models on the same question set is the most informative thing this dialogue can produce.
resumption_hooks.starting_question: Run the exact series of architect probes (with the same prior context: PTSG-Core repository only) on at least three additional LLM providers (Claude, GPT-class, Mistral Large, Llama, etc.). Tabulate which questions yielded matching architectural conclusions and which yielded divergent answers. For divergent answers, identify whether the divergence is (a) a comprehension failure of one or more models, (b) ambiguity in the published documentation, or (c) legitimate alternative valid readings.

resumption_hooks.title: Pushing toward Formation design
resumption_hooks.description: Gemini demonstrated comprehension of the Core; the natural next step is to ask Gemini to design a Formation. This is a stronger test than comprehension — it requires generative architectural design.
resumption_hooks.starting_question: Ask Gemini to draft Layer 1 Chapter 1 ('Scope and Boundary Conditions') for an I²C peripheral Formation that uses PTSG-Core. Constraints: must follow the structural template of PTSG-Core Chapter 1; must specify exactly what external registers, Condition signals, and timing-signal assignments the Formation provides; must satisfy the minimum-stay-count discipline for any background operations the Formation supports; must respect the Core's invariants (no Core modifications proposed). Evaluate the draft for both architectural soundness and Open Prompt format compliance.

resumption_hooks.title: Seeking counter-evidence
resumption_hooks.description: The contributor explicitly invites counter-evidence to the AI-affinity claim. Pose to Gemini deliberately hard or trick questions — questions where the published documentation is genuinely ambiguous, where Chapter 1 leaves room for misinterpretation, where the natural LLM hallucination patterns might surface.
resumption_hooks.starting_question: Compose ten 'stress-test' questions about PTSG-Core that exploit (a) genuine ambiguities in Chapter 1, (b) places where Chapter 1's terminology overlaps with conventional CPU terminology that LLMs may pattern-match incorrectly, (c) edge cases that the documentation does not explicitly address. Pose these to Gemini. Record all responses verbatim, including any hallucinations. Tabulate the failure modes by category and propose corresponding documentation improvements.

resumption_hooks.title: Verifying Gemini's Quartus workflow against current tool behavior
resumption_hooks.description: Phase 11 of the dialogue contains the most consequential claim — that Quartus's Update Memory Initialization File + Assembler-only workflow makes PTSG-Core persistence achievable without re-synthesis. The architect should verify this against current Quartus behavior.
resumption_hooks.starting_question: Execute Gemini's claimed workflow against a real PTSG-Core implementation on actual Quartus tooling: (1) Initial full compile of PTSG-Core + minimal Formation. (2) JTAG-modify the instruction memory in-place. (3) Save modified content as a new .mif file. (4) 'Update Memory Initialization File' Quartus operation. (5) Re-run ONLY the Assembler step (skipping Synthesis and Fitter). (6) Generate .sof/.pof. (7) Time the entire workflow. (8) Confirm that the resulting ROM, when programmed, produces the modified behavior. If any step in Gemini's description fails or requires modification, document and incorporate into the next Chapter 1 revision (or as a Layer 3 deployment-workflow guide).

key_outputs_for_repository: First contributed Layer 2 trace — sets precedent for the contributed/ subdirectory's content quality and schema-adaptation conventions
Cross-provider validation of AI-affinity claim — adds Google Gemini and NotebookLM as data points alongside Anthropic Claude; the claim's support set is no longer single-provider
Empirical observation that Open Prompt scope boundaries are observably visible to LLMs — Gemini correctly demarcates Chapter 1 vs Chapter 2+ vs Tie-decision territory in its language confidence

Discovery of an under-articulated derivation: the Formation-documentation obligation (DP-6) that Chapter 1 § 1.6 implies but does not state. Candidate for inclusion in future CONTRIBUTING.md updates or per-Formation README templates

Empirical workflow inference: the Quartus 'Update MIF + Assembler only' persistence workflow that Gemini derived from the abstract principle 're-synthesis-free reprogrammability'. Awaiting empirical verification (Hook E); if verified, candidate for inclusion as a Layer 3 deployment-workflow guide or Chapter 1 appendix

Schema-adaptation precedent: this trace establishes that contributed traces of subtype 'comprehension demonstration' may adapt the decision_points field to record reconstructed-decisions rather than dialogue-decisions, while preserving full schema compatibility

evidence_status_for_ai_affinity_claim.claim_under_test: PTSG-Core's instruction set is amenable to LLM-based code generation with low hallucination risk; LLM readers of Layers 1+2 can engage at multiple depths simultaneously (Chapter 1 § 1.7).
evidence_status_for_ai_affinity_claim.claim_falsifiability_status: Explicitly stated as a falsifiable working hypothesis in Chapter 1 § 1.7; contributor explicitly invites counter-evidence.

independent_supports_list.data_point: NotebookLM (Google) — complete explanation video generated from Chapter 1 alone

evidence_status_for_ai_affinity_claim.next_falsification_attempt: See Resumption Hook D (stress-test questions) and Hook E (Quartus workflow empirical verification)

closing_note:
The first reader from outside the household; the documentation held.

Boundaries that are visible to humans become boundaries that are visible to LLMs — this is what Open Prompt means.

Falsifiability is not a defect to be hidden; it is the property that makes any evidence-of-support meaningful in the first place.

最初の家外の読者；文書は持ちこたえた。

人間に可視な境界はLLMに可視な境界となる——これがOpen Promptが意味するものである。

反証可能性は隠すべき欠陥ではない；それは支持証拠が意味あるものになる、その性質である。

This trace is released into the public domain under CC0 1.0 Universal by submission. The contributor affirms that all Gemini output preserved herein is verbatim and unaltered, and explicitly invites future readers to seek counter-evidence as vigorously as additional support.

本軌跡は提出によりCC0 1.0 Universalのもとパブリックドメインに公開される。貢献者は、ここに保存されたすべてのGemini出力が逐語的かつ未変更であることを断言し、将来の読者が追加支持と同じく精力的に反証拠を探すことを明示的に招待する。
